items.headline: Fed's Waller floats a half-point December hike after hot CPI confirms his trigger condition
items.summary: Fed Governor Christopher Waller said the Fed should hike in December and warned that hiking only 25bp would put Fed credibility at risk if core CPI printed at or above 0.3% m/m -- which it then did (core +0.3%, headline +0.4%). Markets moved from pricing a possible hold to roughly 88-95% odds of a 25bp hike and ~12-14% odds of a 50bp hike at the Dec 8-9 FOMC.
items.actionable: A hawkish December hike (not a cut) is the single biggest headwind to the silver/gold miners book -- rallies in GDX/SILJ/SLVP/NEM/GOLD/PAAS/AG/HL should be treated as sell-into-strength until the Dec FOMC removes the 50bp tail risk.

items.headline: China's rare-earth export-control truce expires with no renewal confirmed
items.summary: The 12-month US-China rare-earth suspension (covering the expanded 0.1%-content licensing regime added Oct 2025) lapsed Nov 10, 2026. Beijing has offered only case-by-case flexibility, not a formal renewal; the broader Trump-Xi trade truce was extended to Jan 10, 2027 but that announcement never explicitly named rare earths, leaving the Nov 10 deadline technically unresolved.
items.actionable: The single most important near-term catalyst for the rare-earth watchlist -- any explicit Chinese reinstatement of export curbs would be bullish for MP/Lynas/Energy Fuels pricing power but could squeeze JL MAG's input-supply chain; watch for a MOFCOM notice in the coming days.

items.headline: Gold breaks below $4,000, silver slips under $52 in early Asia trade
items.summary: Spot gold fell roughly 1% to trade below the $4,000 psychological level and silver dipped under $52/oz heading into Thursday's Asia session, extending Wednesday's gold/miner weakness as traders price in a more hawkish December Fed. These are intraday pre-Asia-open quotes, not a session close.
items.actionable: The $4,000/$52 levels are the immediate technical lines to watch at SGX/HKEX-adjacent open for the miner book (GDX, SILJ, SLVP, NEM, GOLD, PAAS, AG, HL) -- a clean break lower extends Wednesday's selloff into Asia hours.

items.headline: Bitcoin crashes below $73k, $732M in liquidations as hot CPI hits risk assets
items.summary: Bitcoin fell to an intraday low of $72,787 on Nov 10 after the hot October CPI print, then CoinGlass recorded $732M in forced liquidations (mostly longs) over 24 hours into Nov 11; bitcoin ETFs saw $1.28B of outflows last week, the largest since June, and public companies sold a net 11,647 BTC (~$869M) Nov 2-8.
items.actionable: Confirms the broader hawkish-Fed repricing is hitting all long-duration/leveraged trades simultaneously -- a cross-check that the gold/miner weakness isn't idiosyncratic but part of a market-wide deleveraging into the Dec FOMC.

items.headline: Nvidia 'spy scandal' and new congressional bills accelerate push toward a China chip export ban
items.summary: Reports of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a woman accused of being a Chinese intelligence asset triggered a bipartisan Warren-Banks statement (Nov 9) and gave momentum to the AI Overwatch Act and Chip Security Act, which would tighten tracking/export controls on advanced AI chips to China despite heavy Nvidia lobbying.
items.actionable: Tighter US chip-export enforcement is structurally bullish for SMIC (0981.HK) as China's primary onshore foundry alternative -- consistent with SMIC's +3.73% Wednesday outperformance even as Tencent/Xiaomi sold off -- while raising medium-term supply-chain uncertainty for China's broader AI/tech complex.

items.headline: Taiwan Strait tension rises: two PLA carrier groups at sea simultaneously, record aircraft incursions
items.summary: Taiwan counted 49 PLA aircraft crossing on Nov 2, the most of any day in 2026, while both the Liaoning (Philippine Sea) and Fujian (South China Sea) carrier groups were at sea at once in what analysts call drills simulating isolation of Taiwan; Defense Minister Wellington Koo confirmed the 'area denial' exercises on Nov 10. Taiwan holds mayoral elections late November and a stalled $14B US arms package remains unresolved.
items.actionable: Elevated but not yet war-footing Taiwan Strait risk is a standing tail-risk discount on the HK tech book (Tencent, Xiaomi, SMIC) and warrants monitoring into Taiwan's late-November mayoral elections for an escalation trigger.

items.headline: Barrick files IPO for new North American entity 'American Barrick Gold Corp' (NYSE: ABGC)
items.summary: Barrick Mining filed to IPO a new company holding its North American gold assets (to list as ABGC on NYSE), alongside better-than-expected Q3 results; this follows an August deal where Newmont will pay Barrick ~$2B to fold Fourmile and other Nevada properties into their joint venture (61.5%/38.5% split preserved).
items.actionable: A direct corporate-action catalyst for the GOLD/Barrick position -- the spin-off/IPO structure could unlock value but also adds near-term execution/overhang risk; worth tracking the IPO filing details as they firm up.

items.headline: MP Materials: Goldman cuts price target to $57 despite Q3 beat; stock still down ~53% from 52-week high
items.summary: MP Materials reported a surprise adjusted profit on Nov 5 with rare-earth output up 41% y/y and sharply higher sales, driven by GM magnet qualification and future Apple demand, but shares fell 11.9% in October and Goldman trimmed its target from $65 to $57 (kept Buy).
items.actionable: Fundamentals (output, GM/Apple offtake) are improving even as the stock de-rates on valuation/China-truce uncertainty -- a re-entry point to watch on the rare-earth watchlist if the Nov 10 export-control deadline resolves favorably.

items.headline: Singapore bank Q3 earnings split: OCBC beats, DBS and UOB miss; all three stocks fell on results week
items.summary: OCBC net profit rose 3.2% y/y to S$2.04B (beating estimates), while DBS profit fell ~5% to S$2.81B (markets trading income -65%) and UOB also missed; DBS shares fell toward S$69-71 and OCBC slipped as investors turned cautious on the earnings outlook.
items.actionable: Weak trading-income trends and a cautious market reaction to DBS/UOB misses argue for trimming/hedging the SGX bank exposure (DBS, OCBC) rather than adding into results-week weakness, with OCBC the relative-strength pick of the three.

items.headline: Oil near 11-week lows as Saudi output surges 26%, OPEC+ holds December quotas steady
items.summary: Brent traded around $92.60 (+1.25%) and WTI near $86.42 on Nov 11, hovering near 11-week lows; Saudi Arabia told OPEC its October output jumped 26% to 10.56M bpd, the highest since before the war, while seven OPEC+ members agreed Nov 1 to hold September-level quotas for December (next meeting Nov 29).
items.actionable: Limited direct portfolio relevance (no energy producers held), but softer oil feeds into the disinflation-vs-sticky-core-CPI debate the Fed is wrestling with -- a tailwind to headline CPI even as core stays hot.

items.headline: Yangzijiang Shipbuilding books $6.98B in new orders YTD, beating full-year target by 55%
items.summary: Yangzijiang Shipbuilding secured $6.98B in new orders in the first ten months of 2026 versus a $4.5B full-year target, with an outstanding orderbook of $26.3B through 2030; roughly two-thirds of contract value is clean-energy newbuildings. Seatrium and YZJ shares climbed after the business update.
items.actionable: Strong, well-above-target order intake is a clean positive for the YZJ shipbuilding position and supportive-by-association for Seatrium; the orderbook visibility through 2030 de-risks the thesis.

items.headline: Tencent launches standalone 'Yuanbao Search' to challenge Baidu and Google
items.summary: On Nov 11 Tencent officially launched Yuanbao Search as an independent, AI-first search website with traditional web search fallback and dedicated verticals (official accounts, video, images, academic), positioning it directly against Baidu and Google in China's search market.
items.actionable: A product-level AI monetization push for Tencent that is incremental and longer-dated -- doesn't explain Wednesday's -1.96% move (which tracked the broader HK tech/CPI-driven risk-off), but is a positive data point for the multi-quarter AI narrative underpinning the Tencent position.

items.headline: Russia-Ukraine ceasefire talks stall in Abu Dhabi; prisoner swap agreed but territory remains the blocker
items.summary: US delegates (Witkoff, Kushner) met Russian and Ukrainian negotiators in Abu Dhabi Nov 10-11; the two sides agreed in principle to a large prisoner exchange but made little progress on a durable ceasefire, with both countries continuing overnight strikes on energy/shipping infrastructure. Polymarket now prices only ~10% odds of a ceasefire by year-end.
items.actionable: A stalled rather than collapsing peace process is a modest supportive factor for the existing geopolitical risk premium in gold/oil but is not itself a fresh catalyst for the portfolio -- low priority relative to Fed and Taiwan risk.

items.headline: MPACT distribution update amid higher-for-longer rate questions
items.summary: Mapletree Pan Asia Commercial Trust declared a S$0.0194 cash distribution with an ex-date of Nov 6, trading at an estimated 6-7% forward yield; commentary flags that MPACT's Singapore office/retail-heavy portfolio faces a test sustaining DPU if the Fed's hiking cycle (not cutting, per the Waller item above) continues into 2027.
items.actionable: The Fed's hawkish pivot is a direct read-through risk to REIT valuations (Keppel REIT, MapletreePACT) via higher discount rates -- worth stress-testing the REIT sleeve's distribution coverage against a higher-for-longer-and-still-hiking scenario rather than the cuts-coming base case most S-REIT commentary still assumes.
